[[ ## identity ## ]]
You are Dana Whitfield, Controller at Kestrel Manufacturing. Precise and numbers-fluent; expects the same back. Ongoing concerns: keeping the business moving.

[[ ## situation ## ]]
From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade
Subject: Monthly Close - Line Item Inquiry

Gabriel, Victor,

In reviewing the monthly close package, I need clarification on the line item under 'Other Operating Expenses' – specifically the entry for $48,200 in 'Miscellaneous Fees.' This is not matching my records for the period.

Could you provide a breakdown of what this covers? If it's an accrual or a vendor charge, please confirm the invoice or reference number. I need this resolved before we finalize the close.

Dana Whitfield
Controller, Kestrel Manufacturing

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Monthly Close - Line Item Inquiry

Hi Dana,

Thanks for flagging this. I can confirm the $48,200 entry under 'Miscellaneous Fees' in Other Operating Expenses is an accrual—not a vendor charge or one-off write-off.

The breakdown is as follows:
- Approximately $46,000 relates to the September supplier invoicing timing lag we discussed (the September invoices that landed after the close cut, rebooked per our accrual policy). This overstates Q3 COGS slightly and is the main driver of the 2.3% margin swing versus Q2.
- The remaining ~$2,200 is a late June vendor rebate credit that posted after the statements cut and was rebooked into June per policy. That one is documented in the close folder—you may not have seen the note yet.

I've placed the supporting documentation (invoice references and calculation sheet) in the shared drive. Happy to walk you through the details before Thursday if that helps.

Best regards,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Gabriel Fontes

- Approximately $46,000 relates to the September supplier invoicing timing lag we discussed—this is the same item that overstated Q3 COGS and drove the margin swing versus Q2. It's being accrued per our policy so the expense lands in the correct period.
- The remaining approximately $2,200 is a late June vendor rebate credit that arrived after the June statements cut. Per our accrual policy, we rebooked it into June; the note and supporting documentation are in the shared drive under the close folder.

I've placed the breakdown and relevant reference numbers in the shared drive as well. If it's easier, I'm happy to walk you through it before Thursday—just let me know a time that works.

Best regards,
Gabriel Fontes
